notes.caliber_separation: The fulfillment ratio is a dimensionless ratio on the library caliber; f_Q_deliv is an absolute m^-2 quantity on the descriptive delivered caliber. They are different quantities at different calibers: report them in separate statements with their own tags, never side by side in one table and never as a ratio of one to the other.
notes.dip_attribution: Both R2F dips come from the greedy anchor construction, which is deterministic and reproducible. Evidence: in all 180 R2F and R3H sweep units the anchor equals the unit maximum (max_f1_star == anchor_f1_star) and the search-only maximum is empty, so no dip can be a search miss. Each dip is the net of two opposite single-seed displacements (see the dip.* entries for the exact seeds). No physical monotonicity claim is made from either dip.
notes.falsified_direction_claim: A direction claim linking higher coverage to lower fulfillment is NOT registered and must not be written: on the L8 data the pooled coefficient is positive (see relation.*), and the per-family values are mixed. Only the coefficient and its sample size are reported.
notes.infeasible_semantics: R1C at s=0.8 is not a zero-coverage point: all ten seeds exited 11, meaning the family admits no feasible individual at that tightening. It is a different statement from 'the search found nothing to serve' and the two must be written differently.
notes.manifest_provenance: The aggregate loads scenario manifests from experiments/v4_results/scenarios; the v5 copies are byte-identical (80/80 sha256 equal, checked in the phase-1 receipt). The ledger's readings are therefore unaffected, but the path in build_sweep_results.py is a latent provenance trap: if the scenario copies ever diverge, the aggregate would silently read the v4 manifest.
notes.str_floor: STR delivers the library floor (2.4669 m) regardless of the order; tightening the order there is a floor step, not a continuous degradation. f_Q_deliv has no STR domain.
notes.unit_of_demand: 477,308 counts served task instances summed over every tie-set record (9,430 records over 260 units at nine demand points). It is not a count of distinct tasks.
